newsitem.title: USA: HarCor Energy proven reserves increased.
newsitem.headline: HarCor Energy proven reserves increased.

text.p: HarCor Energy Inc on Wednesday said its proven reserves consisted of 14.9 million barrels of crude oil and natural gas liquids and 95.5 billion cubic feet of natural gas.
Those figures were net of a December 1996 sale of 336,000 barrels of oil and .313 BCF of natural gas.

The future discounted cash flow valued of its reserves (pre-tax, discounted at 10 percent or "NPV 10 percent") increased to $261 million in 1996 from $124.5 million in 1995. Oil and gas prices used at year-end 1996 in determining NPV 10% value were $23.77 per barrel and $3.00 per MMBtu.

During 1996, HarCor produced 523,000 barrels of crude oil, 232,000 barrels of natural gas liquids and 5.8 BCF of natural gas. On an oil equivalent basis, total production averaged 4,714 barrels of oil equivalent per day for 1996.

Also in 1996, HarCor added 656,000 barrels of crude oil and natural gas liquids and 14.0 BCF of natural gas or three million barrels of oil equivalent, representing a production replacement rate of 174 percent.
HarCor said its probable reserves totaled 2.656 million barrels of oil and 7.982 BCF of natural gas.

Approximately 51 percent of the probable oil reserves and 23 percent of the probable gas reserves are additional waterflood probable reserves which are dependent on the performance of HarCor's recently initiated waterflood program in California and could eventually be classified as proven.
HarCor is an energy company engaged in the acquisition, exploitation and exploration of onshore crude oil and natural gas properties in the United States.
